You are writing a eulogy for your brother, Jason Wilson, who passed away last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center, at age 67.

User request:
You have been entrusted with the honor of delivering a eulogy for Jason Wilson, a beloved brother, friend, and community member. Your task is to write a speech that captures the essence of Jason's life, celebrates his legacy, and provides comfort to the diverse group of mourners gathered to bid him farewell. Jason deceased at age 67, last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center.
Your audience will include family members, friends, colleagues, and acquaintances from Jason's life. They are a mix of various ages and backgrounds, united in their grief and respect for Jason. Your speech should resonate with this diverse group, bringing them together in remembrance and celebration of Jason's life.

answer:
Thank you all for being here to remember my brother, Jason Wilson.

Jason passed away last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center. He was 67 years old. Those words are difficult to say, and harder still to take in. Even now, part of me expects another conversation with him—another chance to hear his voice, to ask him something, or simply to spend a little more time together.

Being his brother was part of my life long before I understood how precious that bond would become. A brother belongs to your history in a particular way. He remembers people and places with you. He knows earlier versions of you. And when he is gone, you feel the loss in the present, but also across all the years you shared.

I will miss Jason in ways I can name today, and in ways I will discover later. There will be moments when I reach for the phone before remembering. There will be things I wish I could tell him. I know many of you will have those moments, too.

Looking around this room, I am reminded that my brother’s life reached far beyond the part I shared with him. Some of you knew Jason as family. Others knew him as a friend, a colleague, or a familiar presence in the community. Each of you carries memories that belong to your relationship with him: a conversation, a shared experience, perhaps an ordinary day that has become precious now.

I hope we keep telling those stories. Even the small ones. Especially the small ones. They help us remember a person fully—the voice, the expressions, the habits, the things that could make us laugh. There is room for that laughter here, alongside our tears.

Sixty-seven years cannot be gathered neatly into one speech. And I cannot speak for everything Jason meant to everyone here. But your presence says something that words alone cannot: his life mattered to you. You have come because there is something about him you will carry forward.

In the days ahead, we may grieve differently. Some of us will want company; others will need quiet. Some will find comfort in faith, some in memories, and some in the simple kindness of someone sitting beside them. We do not have to find the same words or follow the same path to care for one another.

Today, I am grateful that we can be here together. Grateful to those who cared for Jason, and to everyone who has offered comfort to our family. Your kindness has given us something to lean on.

Jason, I wish we had more time. I wish there were another ordinary afternoon ahead of us, another conversation with no reason to think it might be the last.

Thank you for being my brother. I love you. I will miss you, and I will keep your memory close.
